steps.body: Compare 3-digit numbers by walking the spots left to right: hundreds first. The first spot where they differ decides everything — 275 and 312: 2 < 3, so 275 < 312.
Open the first place that differs.

widget.prompt: Line up 275 and 312. Inspect the first place that decides which number is greater.

choices.label: Hundreds place
choices.feedback: Yes. The hundreds are 2 and 3, so the comparison is decided right away.

choices.label: Tens place
choices.feedback: The hundreds already differ, so there is no need to use the tens.

choices.label: Ones place
choices.feedback: Start at the greatest place. The hundreds decide before the ones are reached.

widget.successFeedback: The hundreds place decides: 3 hundreds is more than 2 hundreds, so 312 is greater.
widget.explorationFeedback: Open the hundreds stage before choosing the deciding place.
widget.fallbackFeedback: Compare from left to right. The hundreds differ first: 2 hundreds and 3 hundreds.

predict.prompt: 275 and 312 differ in the first digit. Which place do you expect to decide the comparison?
predict.reveal: The aligned place chart opens at the hundreds: 2 hundreds versus 3 hundreds. That first difference makes 312 greater.

widget.gtFeedback: Check the hundreds digit first: 2 is less than 3, so 275 < 312, not >.
widget.eqFeedback: These numbers aren't equal — the hundreds digits already differ: 2 vs 3.
widget.successFeedback: Yes — the hundreds digits differ first: 2 < 3, so 275 < 312.

widget.prompt: Team Sun scored 512 points. Team Moon scored 489 points. Compare their scores: <, =, or >?
widget.ltFeedback: Check the hundreds digit: 5 is greater than 4, so 512 > 489, not <.
widget.eqFeedback: These numbers aren't equal — the hundreds digits already differ: 5 vs 4.

steps.body: If the hundreds match, move to the tens spot. If those also match, the ones spot breaks the tie.

widget.prompt: The parking lot had 431 cars in the morning and 468 cars by noon. Compare morning and noon: <, =, or >?
widget.gtFeedback: Hundreds are tied at 4. Check the tens digit: 3 < 6, so 431 < 468, not >.
widget.eqFeedback: Hundreds match, but the tens digits differ (3 vs 6) — not equal.
widget.successFeedback: Yes — hundreds match (4=4), so check tens: 3 < 6, meaning 431 < 468.

steps.body: A big first digit can still lose — bigger digits later can't fight back. 399 vs 401: hundreds 3 < 4 settles it instantly, no need to check further.
A big digit later doesn't help.

widget.prompt: 399 has two big 9s. 401 has none. Compare 399 and 401 anyway: <, =, or >?
widget.gtFeedback: 399's big 9s can't outweigh a smaller hundreds digit: 3 < 4, so 399 < 401.
widget.eqFeedback: The hundreds digits already differ (3 vs 4) — not equal.
widget.successFeedback: Yes — hundreds: 3 < 4 settles it right away, no matter what the other digits are.

steps.body: Compare when hundreds AND tens match.
explanationVariants: Hundreds and tens match; ones settle it: 4 < 7, so 234 < 237.
The ones spot breaks the tie.

widget.prompt: 234 and 237 share the same hundreds digit and the same tens digit. Compare them: <, =, or >?
widget.successFeedback: Yes — hundreds (2=2) and tens (3=3) match, so ones decide: 4 < 7, meaning 234 < 237.
widget.gtFeedback: Hundreds and tens are tied. Check the ones: 4 < 7, so 234 < 237, not >.
widget.eqFeedback: Hundreds and tens match, but the ones differ (4 vs 7) — not equal.

explanationVariants: When all spots match, the numbers are equal.

widget.prompt: Bin A holds 500 blocks. Bin B holds 500 blocks. Compare the two bins: <, =, or >?
widget.ltFeedback: These numbers are identical in every spot — they're equal, not less than.
widget.gtFeedback: These numbers are identical in every spot — they're equal, not greater than.

explanationVariants: Check spot by spot until you find a difference.

widget.prompt: A ticket line has 685 people. A second line has 619 people. Compare the two lines: <, =, or >?
widget.successFeedback: Yes — hundreds match (6=6), tens decide: 8 > 1, so 685 > 619.
widget.ltFeedback: Hundreds are tied. Check the tens digit: 8 > 1, so 685 > 619, not <.
widget.eqFeedback: Hundreds match, but the tens digits differ (8 vs 1) — not equal.

hints: Compare the hundreds digit first: 6 = 6, tied.
Move to the tens digit: 8 vs 1.

steps.body: Compare 3-digit numbers spot by spot, left to right — the first difference decides everything.
takeaways: Check hundreds first; if tied, check tens; if still tied, check ones.
A bigger digit later can't outweigh a smaller digit earlier.
If every spot matches, the numbers are equal.

concept.body: Compare 3-digit numbers spot by spot, left to right: hundreds first, then tens, then ones. The first spot where they differ decides the comparison.
